- [USER] User expressed interest in the historical events that have shaped the relationship between Parliament and the monarchy in Britain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Magna Carta (1215) limited the power of the monarchy and established that the king was subject to the law.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Civil War (1642-1651) solidified the power of Parliament over the monarchy, leading to the execution of King Charles I.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Glorious Revolution (1688) marked the beginning of the constitutional monarchy in Britain.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Reform Act (1832) expanded voting eligibility and increased the power of the House of Commons relative to the House of Lords.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Queen's Speech (1911) limited the powers of the House of Lords and established conditions under which the monarch could refuse royal assent.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Royal Marriages Act (1772) required royal family members to obtain the monarch's permission to marry.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The relationship between Parliament and the monarchy is characterized by a delicate balance of power and influence.
